research.query: Is CO2 a good fire suppressant in space?
research.answer:
The question was matched to: suppressant. Below is what the indexed documents state about it, quoted with their sources.

**Evidence**
- CO2 mole fraction. Test condition recorded in PSI tables (-). FLEX: 274 values, 0–0.7 -. [S10]
- Helium mole fraction. Test condition recorded in PSI tables (-). FLEX: 274 values, 0–0.45 -; CFI: 87 values, 0–0.59 -. [S11]
- FLEX: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for… [S1]
- FLEX: FLEX compares CO2 and helium as gaseous suppressants. At 21 % O2, share of FLEX tests ending in flame extinction before burnout by atmosphere — N2 only: 14/29; CO2: 13/18; He: 7/7. FLEX varied CO2 up to 0.7 and He up to 0.45 mole fraction. Which inert agent and which… [S2]
- ACME CFI-G: 4. Identify or develop a chemical kinetics mechanism that yields good agreement between the CFD predictions and the ISS measurements. [S3]
- BASS: BASS Burning and Suppression of Solids. Spacecraft Fire Safety. Microgravity Science Glovebox [S4]
- DAFT / DAFT-2: A Research Plan for Fire Prevention, Detection and Suppression in Crewed Exploration Systems; Detection of Smoke from Microgravity Fires [S5]
- Dust can look like smoke to a particle counter: DAFT showed that a modified commercial particle counter could be used in microgravity, measuring a test dust aerosol released on the ISS. Limitation: Terrestrial test dust, not lunar regolith; feasibility test only. [S12]
- BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. Limitation: Outcome annotations  [S13]

**Limits**
- Extractive answer (no language model configured): passages are quoted, not interpreted.
- Only documents in this knowledge base were searched.

sources.title: FLEX — Flame Extinguishment Experiment — objective
sources.text: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions. The mission seeks to validate and improve simplified models by incorporating detailed chemical reactions, heat transfer, and material movement, using both space-based data and extensive ground-based tests. Key flight experiment goals include obtaining high-resolution measurements of droplet burning rates, flame extinction behavior, heat radiation, soot levels, and temperature profiles, while systematically analyzing the effects of different ambient conditions and suppressant concentrations.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.

sources.title: More oxygen: droplet flames more often survive to burnout
sources.text: FLEX droplet tests in N2-only atmospheres that ended in flame extinction before burnout — Heptane: 5/17 at 21 % O2 vs 0/11 at 30–34 % O2; Methanol: 9/12 at 21 % O2 vs 2/13 at 30–34 % O2. Remaining tests ended in burnout ('completion') or droplet disruption. Limitation: Isolated droplets, two fuels; 'extinction' here means the flame went out before the droplet was consumed (often radiative), not the action of an extinguisher. Counts, not a model.

top_passage.text: The sooting tendencies of the more fuel-rich flames will be investigated using soot luminosity and laser extinction measurements to determine soot temperatures and soot volume fractions. Flame temperatures in non-sooting regions will be measured using thin-filament pyrometry.
